subject: Private offer: usage smoothing, reseller cushion & rollback protection
messages:
From: Alexa Moore <alexa@tidalcloud.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai; procurement@tidalcloud.com
Cc: CloudBridge Partnerships <partners@cloudbridge.io>
Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private offer: usage smoothing ask

Hi Ben / team,

Thanks for the demo last week — TidalCloud is excited by the latency/cost profile you showed. Procurement asked me to follow up with a couple of specifics for the private offer so we can brief legal and our reseller (CloudBridge):

1) Usage smoothing: can Redwood apply a 3-month smoothing window so our monthly overages don’t spike the committed tiers? We need predictable billing cadence for our finance team.
2) Reseller cushion: CloudBridge asked for a 5-7% margin protection on list price (they resell to end customers). We need to understand whether that should be handled as list price floor, passback, or a one-time rebate.
3) Rollback protection: if our usage drops below committed baseline in month 2 or 3, can we avoid retroactive true-ups that hit our AMs?

Procurement will need a draft PO and a sample private-offer offer letter by end of next week. I attached our standard procurement checklist — happy to hop on a call.

Thanks,
Alexa
Alexa Moore
Head of Cloud Procurement
TidalCloud
[Attachment: TidalCloud_Procurement_Checklist.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alexa Moore <alexa@tidalcloud.com>
Cc: procurement@tidalcloud.com, partners@cloudbridge.io, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private offer: usage smoothing ask

Alexa — great to hear and thanks for the clear list. Quick answers and proposed next steps below.

Short answers:
- Usage smoothing: yes — we can implement a 3-month rolling smoothing for metered usage within the private offer. That will show up as an invoiced smoothing adjustment (applied monthly) rather than an immediate downgrade of committed tier.
- Reseller cushion: we recommend handling this as a reseller passback (one-time quarterly settlement) instead of lowering the list price. That preserves our published list while letting CloudBridge capture margin.
- Rollback protection: we can add a clause that prevents retroactive true-ups for the first 90 days post-contract effective date (subject to a minimum true-up floor — see suggested wording in the attached draft).

Next steps: I attached a working private-offer draft and a pricing calc (v2) that shows the impact of three approaches: list discount, quarterly rebate, and commit-tier smoothing. Can we do a 30-minute call Monday to walk the numbers with procurement + CloudBridge?

Proposed times: Mon 8/17 9:00–11:00 PT or 14:00–16:00 PT. Let me know what works and I’ll send a calendar invite + HubSpot update.

Best,
Ben Carter
Senior Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0189
[Attachments: TidalCloud_PrivateOffer_Draft.pdf, tidal_pricing_calc_v2.xlsx]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: alexa@tidalcloud.com, procurement@tidalcloud.com, partners@cloudbridge.io
Date: Sun, 16 Aug 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private offer: usage smoothing ask

Looping in a couple of implementation notes from a pricing/ops POV so Alexa and procurement have visibility before the call: 

- Margin waterfall: if CloudBridge needs 5–7% margin protection, we can structure it as a quarterly passback tied to net realized revenue after marketplace fees. Advantage: keeps list price intact and avoids marketplace SKU changes.
- Minimum economics: to avoid erosion, require a list-price floor (e.g., no more than 10% off published list in aggregate across discounts + passbacks). If procurement prefers guaranteed lower unit price to end customers, we need to model the delta.
- Accounting / invoicing: smoothing will create negative/positive invoice adjustments month-to-month — ops prefers explicit fields on the invoice ("smoothing adjustment", "reseller passback") to keep GL clean.
- Alternative: one-time onboarding credit for first 3 months (non-recurring) instead of permanent margin carve; often accepted by resellers as it funds initial GTM.

I added a short scenario table to the pricing calc (tab: "Reseller cushion scenarios"). Ben — I’ll be on the call Monday and can walk the waterfall.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Marketplace Partnerships | Redwood Inference
[karthik_iyer@redwood.ai]

Thanks Ben/Karthik — that all looks reasonable. A couple of clarifications before the call: 

- CloudBridge prefers a quarterly passback tied to "net realized" revenue (post-marketplace fee) — that aligns with their commercial model. Please confirm that the passback can be automated on Redwood's side (booked as a settlement line item).
- Procurement: our target is to execute the PO by 8/27. We need the private-offer letter + a sample PO template and a DocuSign path.

We’ll take the Mon 8/17 10:00 PT slot — please send the invite. Also, please share the HubSpot deal link in the calendar invite.

Alexa

Head of Cloud Procurement | TidalCloud

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai; alexa@tidalcloud.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai; procurement@tidalcloud.com
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private offer: usage smoothing ask

Alexa / team — thanks for the call earlier (great progress). A couple legal/finance bullets to finalize before PO: 

- Wording for smoothing: "Customer usage will be averaged over a rolling 3-month period for the purposes of committed tier calculation. Smoothing adjustments will be invoiced monthly and are non-recurring adjustments to reflect averaged consumption."
- Reseller passback clause: "Seller (Redwood) will calculate a quarterly reseller settlement equal to X% of net realized revenue attributable to orders channeled through the named reseller (CloudBridge). Settlement will be issued as a credit memo applied to the Customer's next invoice. Net realized revenue is defined as gross revenue less marketplace fees and taxes."
- No-retroactive-true-up window: propose 90 days from effective date; exceptions for gross misuse/fraud.
- Tax/treatment: passbacks issued as credit memo to the customer; any tax consequences are the customer's responsibility. We can add alternate language if TidalCloud requires reseller-facing invoices.

I attached a clean private-offer template with the above language inserted and a redline for the PO template. Ben/ops: please review the invoice field names so finance can reconcile.

Irene Choi
Head of Contracts & Billing | Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.ai
